messages:
Kai: Quick idea for a minimal residency handshake: resident region handles writes. If it fails, runtime can accept a short-lived 'residency-token' that explicitly lists allowed fallback regions and allowed features. Token must be signed by control-plane KMS.

Rina: Agree. Keep token tiny: {tenant, allowed_regions, max_tokens, exp, nonce}. Runtime verifies signature + nonce once.

Victor: Ops: we need admission control to avoid thundering herd. Per-tenant concurrency cap + global pool quota. Return 429 with X-Fallback-Reason: capacity when denied.

Maya: Product: expose degraded feature list in tenant settings and make fallback opt-in. Also show in the UI when a request used a fallback (for audit).

ops-bot: ops-bot: reminder: schedule canary guest-pool:v0.5 -> limited-pool on 2024-07-01T02:00Z

Rina: Propose headers: "X-Residency-Mode: resident|fallback" and "X-Residency-Token: <signed>". For guarded tenants, runtime 403s without valid token.

Kai: Local curl example:
```
curl -H "X-Residency-Token: eyJhbGci..." https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

Victor: Metrics: fallback_granted_total{tenant}, fallback_denied_total, fallback_p95_latency. Alert if fallback_granted > 1% of traffic for a tenant in 5m.

Maya: Legal flagged model weight isolation and audit retention. We'll require per-call trace id + token id in logs.

Kai: Edge case: tenant pins to a model unavailable in fallback region. Runtime should consult a small fallback map and either map to compatible variant or return FBACK_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE with suggested alternatives. Document mapping per model family.

Rina: Action items: Rina write token RFC (Mon), Victor run load sim + admission plan (Wed), Maya add opt-in UI + docs (Tue), Legal to draft short addendum (Fri). Ping when RFC ready.

Kai: No objections. Thanks.
